## Declarations and implementations

```plato

//==
// # Blend and growth surfaces

// A ring Dupin cyclide: the image of a torus under an inversion, and the
// classical CAD blend surface — every parameter line is a circle. Requires
// MajorRadius > MinorRadius > 0; Offset is the cyclide's d parameter, and equal
// radii collapse the construction back to an ordinary torus
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dupin_cyclide).
type DupinCyclide
    implements IParametricSurface
{
    MajorRadius: Number;
    MinorRadius: Number;
    Offset: Number;
}

// A logarithmic-spiral shell: a circular section of radius TubeRadius carried
// around TurnCount turns of a spiral that tapers to a point while rising by
// Height, wrapping a columella of radius InnerRadius
// (https://mathworld.wolfram.com/SeashellSurface.html).
type SeashellSurface
    implements IParametricSurface
{
    TurnCount: Number;
    Height: Number;
    TubeRadius: Number;
    InnerRadius: Number;
}

// A radial harmonic surface: the radius is a sum of four powered sinusoids in
// the two spherical angles, Frequencies holding the four frequencies and
// Exponents the four matching exponents. The eight-number family behind the
// familiar lobed blobs (https://paulbourke.net/geometry/sphericalh/).
type SphericalHarmonicSurface
    implements IParametricSurface
{
    Frequencies: Number4;
    Exponents: Number4;
}

//==
// # Non-orientable and self-intersecting surfaces
//
// The classical immersions: surfaces that cannot be embedded in 3D without
// crossing themselves, so every type here denotes an immersed image rather than
// an embedded shape. Self-intersections are part of the definition, not an
// artefact of the parameterization, and none of these surfaces has a
// well-defined inside.

//==
// # One-sided surfaces

// The figure-eight immersion of the Klein bottle: a section of radius TubeRadius
// makes a half turn as it travels once around a ring of radius Radius, so the
// surface closes onto itself reversed. Closed and one-sided, with no boundary
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Klein_bottle).
type KleinBottle
    implements IParametricSurface
{
    Radius: Number;
    TubeRadius: Number;
}

// The Roman surface of Steiner: the image of the sphere of radius 1 under
// (x, y, z) -> Scale * (y z, z x, x y). A model of the real projective plane
// with three segments of self-intersection meeting at a triple point
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_surface).
type RomanSurface
    implements IParametricSurface
{
    Scale: Number;
}

// The cross-cap: the projective plane immersed with a single segment of
// self-intersection ending in two pinch points, scaled by Radius
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-cap).
type CrossCap
    implements IParametricSurface
{
    Radius: Number;
}

// Boy's surface in Apery's parameterization: an immersion of the real projective
// plane with no pinch points, so unlike the Roman surface and the cross-cap it
// is smooth everywhere (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy%27s_surface).
type BoySurface
    implements IParametricSurface
{
    Scale: Number;
}

//==
// # Self-intersecting patches

// Whitney's umbrella (u v, u, v^2), with (u, v) sweeping Domain. The normal form
// of a stable map singularity: a self-intersecting sheet ending in one pinch
// point at the origin (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitney_umbrella).
type WhitneyUmbrella
    implements IParametricSurface
{
    Domain: Bounds2D;
}

// The Bohemian dome: a circle of radius CircleRadius carried around an ellipse
// with semi-axes EllipseRadii, both traversed once. A quartic surface that meets
// itself in two ellipses (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bohemian_dome).
type BohemianDome
    implements IParametricSurface
{
    EllipseRadii: Number2;
    CircleRadius: Number;
}

// Plucker's conoid (the cylindroid): the right conoid whose horizontal rays
// through the Z axis rise as Height * sin(FoldCount * theta), out to Radius. A
// FoldCount of 2 is the classical two-fold conoid
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pl%C3%BCcker%27s_conoid).
type PluckerConoid
    implements IParametricSurface
{
    Radius: Number;
    Height: Number;
    FoldCount: Integer;
}

//==
// # Minimal and pseudospherical surfaces
//
// The two families that differential geometry names after their curvature: the
// minimal surfaces, whose mean curvature vanishes everywhere, and the
// pseudospherical surfaces, whose Gaussian curvature is a negative constant.
// Most are patches over a rectangle of parameters rather than closed shapes, so
// each carries the `Domain` or interval it is cut from; several have
// preconditions on that domain, stated at the type.

//==
// # Minimal surfaces

// Enneper's minimal surface (u - u^3/3 + u v^2, v - v^3/3 + v u^2, u^2 - v^2)
// over Domain, scaled by Scale. Minimal everywhere, and self-intersecting once
// the parameter disc grows past radius sqrt 3
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enneper_surface).
type EnneperSurface
    implements IParametricSurface
{
    Scale: Number;
    Domain: Bounds2D;
}

// Scherk's first surface, z = Scale * ln(cos(y / Scale) / cos(x / Scale)) over
// Domain: the doubly periodic minimal surface. Precondition: Domain stays
// strictly inside the square on which both cosines are positive
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scherk_surface).
type ScherkSurface
    implements IParametricSurface
{
    Scale: Number;
    Domain: Bounds2D;
}
```
